goal: Introduces assert_true()/assert_false() helpers in the test framework and mechanically replaces assert_equal(x, True/False) with them across ~90 functional test files.
Goal is to make boolean assertions easier to scan by removing the redundant equals-to-what comparison.
reviewability: Ready to review now, no rebase or CI issues.
Author actively responded to review feedback and fixed a correctness slip in the helper via force-push.
agreement: Mixed lukewarm support: l0rinc does not object to the change but suggested renaming to truthy/falsy and adding meta-tests for the new helpers (l0rinc).
maflcko is only weakly in favor, calling the real motivation code-bloat reduction rather than the stated rationale, saying they are '~0' on it but raising no objection (maflcko).
The naming disagreement was not adopted by the author, so it stands as an acknowledged but non-blocking drawback.

result.summary: This PR adds assert_true() and assert_false() helpers to the functional test framework and performs a scripted-diff replacing assert_equal(expr, True/False) call sites with the new, more readable helpers across roughly 90 functional test files. It also fixes a pre-existing edge case in a 3-arg assert_equal() call and removes now-unused imports. The change is purely mechanical/cosmetic and does not alter test behavior or coverage.
result.problem: Functional test code that writes assert_equal(expr, True) forces the reader to parse an extra comparison operand to figure out the intent; assert_true()/assert_false() reduce that cognitive overhead for test authors and reviewers scanning test files.

open_concerns: l0rinc suggested renaming assert_true/assert_false to truthy/falsy to accurately describe their non-strict-equality behavior, and requested small meta-tests demonstrating the helpers' behavior; neither was implemented, though l0rinc did not treat this as blocking.
maflcko views the stated rationale (assert being droppable in optimized mode) as beside the point and considers the real benefit merely code-bloat reduction, expressing only lukewarm ('~0') support.
resolved_concerns: l0rinc caught that an early implementation used != True/False, which subtly changed correctness versus truthy/falsy checks; author fixed this via force-push using 'is not' and demonstrated correctness with a manual test-runner patch.

result.card: This PR adds assert_true()/assert_false() helpers to the functional test framework and mechanically replaces roughly 500 assert_equal(x, True/False) call sites across ~90 functional test files with them, aiming to make boolean assertions easier to scan. It is purely a readability refactor with no behavioral, coverage, or performance change, so it is P4 (cleanup) in the tests category and not a genuine member of any other area despite touching files across wallet, p2p, rpc, mempool, mining, and ipc tests only mechanically. Review is Ready: the author already fixed a real correctness slip (assert_equal(..., True) subtly differs from truthy checks) that l0rinc caught, via a force-push using 'is not'. Agreement is Positive w/ caveats: l0rinc suggested renaming to truthy/falsy for accuracy and wants meta-tests, which the author has not adopted, while maflcko is only weakly supportive ('~0'), viewing the real benefit as reduced code bloat. No dependencies; it does not block or unblock other work.
